responses.sql: SELECT SUM(rebtotal) AS total_rebate, AVG(feerate - rebrate) AS avg_net_fee_rate FROM fees WHERE rebrate > 0.0005

assumptions.assumption: Rows where feerate is NULL are excluded from the average, since feerate - rebrate is NULL for them. Rows with a NULL rebtotal are skipped in the sum. The two aggregates may therefore cover slightly different rows.

responses.sql: SELECT SUM(rebtotal) AS total_rebate, AVG(feerate - rebrate) AS avg_net_fee_rate FROM fees WHERE rebrate > 0.0005

assumptions.assumption: Rows where feerate is NULL are excluded from the average (feerate - rebrate is NULL) but their rebtotal still counts toward the sum, since each aggregate ignores missing values independently.

responses.sql: SELECT SUM(rebtotal) AS total_rebate, AVG(feerate - rebrate) AS avg_net_fee_rate FROM fees WHERE rebrate > 0.0005

assumptions.assumption: Rows where feerate is NULL are excluded from the average, because feerate - rebrate is NULL for them. Rows with a NULL rebtotal are still counted in the average if feerate is present. Both follow from ignoring missing values.
SUM and AVG return NULL when no rows match, which is the 'empty' result the request asks for.
